headline: Asian trading was quiet before this week's run of central-bank decisions: the yen slipped again as stocks rose, and the Aussie and kiwi edged up before tonight's Australian inflation figures and New Zealand rate decision.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar held near 102 on the dollar index through Asian trading, a touch firmer against the yen and slightly softer against the Aussie and kiwi. Investors are waiting for Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision, with US durable goods orders and consumer confidence coming first.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Since the US–Iran war began in February, high oil has kept US inflation up, and markets expect the Federal Reserve to hold rates on Wednesday and raise them in December, which supports the dollar. What changed: Little overnight. The dollar index edged up to about 102.04 from 102.00 at Monday's New York close, its gain coming mostly against the yen as Asian stocks rose. Oil eased about half a percent, and the 10-year Treasury yield held near 4.99%. There was no US data overnight. What it means: With the Fed decision a day away, investors are holding positions rather than adding to them, and the dollar is keeping Monday's gains. The question to keep asking: does Fed chair Jerome Powell keep a December hike clearly on the table on Wednesday?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US durable goods orders for September at 7:30 AM CT (about +0.6% expected) and Conference Board consumer confidence at 9:00 AM CT (about 81.2 expected). The Fed decides at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday, with Powell's press conference at 1:30 PM CT; a hold is priced at about 93%.

scenarios.base: The dollar stays near 102 on the index through Tuesday, with the Fed hold and a December hint already priced.
scenarios.bull: Strong durable goods orders and consumer confidence lift short-term yields and push the index above 102.2.
scenarios.bear: Weak US figures or a drop in oil trim December hike bets and pull the index back toward 101.7.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro was flat near $1.117 in Asian trading, with no euro-area news overnight. France's budget vote on revenues, once set for Tuesday, has been postponed, and the European Central Bank decides on Thursday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: France's debt, a budget fight and street protests pushed its 10-year borrowing cost above 5% last week and weighed on the euro, until Moody's kept France's credit rating unchanged late Friday. What changed: Nothing new from Europe overnight. The euro held near $1.1174, just below Monday's close of $1.1178, after a better German business survey on Monday failed to outlast the dollar's afternoon gains. What it means: The euro is drifting with the dollar until the ECB speaks. Calmer French bonds and a stronger German outlook support the case for an ECB hike in December. The question to keep asking: does ECB President Christine Lagarde keep a December hike open on Thursday?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: euro-area money supply figures at 4:00 AM CT Tuesday, then Germany's GfK consumer climate survey at 2:00 AM CT Wednesday. The ECB decides on Thursday at 8:15 AM CT, with Lagarde's press conference at about 8:45 AM CT; a hold is expected.

scenarios.base: The euro stays near $1.117 into Thursday's ECB decision.
scenarios.bull: Steady French bonds and firm euro-area figures lift the euro back above $1.12.
scenarios.bear: Strong US data or a new French budget scare push the euro below $1.115.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound held near $1.334 in Asian trading as UK shop prices rose faster than expected. The British Retail Consortium's index showed the quickest rise in about two and a half years, a day before Chancellor John Healey's first UK Budget.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: A Bank of England rate hike on November 5 is all but priced because UK inflation is running hot, and the pound reached its strongest against the euro since May 2025 on Friday. What changed: The British Retail Consortium said shop prices rose 2.1% from a year earlier in October, up from 1.4% in September and above the 1.6% expected. Food prices rose faster, and so did prices for non-food goods, as shops passed on higher energy, transport and wage costs. The pound barely moved, near $1.3341. What it means: Prices in shops are rising at their quickest pace since early 2024, a sign that energy costs are spreading into everyday goods. That keeps pressure on the Bank of England to raise rates, which supports the pound, but traders are waiting for the Budget before taking big positions. The question to keep asking: does the Budget calm or rattle UK bond markets?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: no UK figures Tuesday; the UK Budget is on Wednesday, around 7:30 AM CT. The Bank of England decides on November 5, where a hike is about 94% priced.
numbers: BRC shop prices (Oct) +2.1% y/y vs 1.6% expected; Sep 1.4%

scenarios.base: The pound stays near $1.334 until Wednesday's Budget.
scenarios.bull: Firm price data and a Budget that keeps borrowing in check let the pound recover toward $1.34.
scenarios.bear: Talk of heavier borrowing before the Budget pushes UK bond yields up for the wrong reasons and the pound below $1.33.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The yen slipped again in Asian trading, with the dollar up about 0.1% to near ¥157.7, as Japanese stocks rose and investors needed less safety. Japan's services prices came in as expected.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Japan imports nearly all its energy, so high oil has weighed on the yen this year; a global stock wobble briefly lifted it last week, with the dollar near ¥156.1. What changed: Japan's Nikkei 225 stock index rose about 1.7%, led by chipmakers, which cut demand for the yen as a safe place for money. Prices firms charge each other for services rose 3.7% from a year earlier in September, as expected; without international shipping the pace eased, so much of the strength is freight costs, not home-grown price pressure. The dollar rose to about ¥157.7 from ¥157.5. What it means: The figures give the Bank of Japan no new push before Friday's decision. Until it signals a December hike more clearly, the wide gap with US rates keeps weighing on the yen on calm days. The question to keep asking: does the Bank of Japan point clearly to December on Friday?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Tokyo consumer prices at 6:30 PM CT Wednesday, then the Bank of Japan decision on Friday, Japan time (late Thursday night CT), where a hold is expected with new forecasts.
numbers: Japan services prices (Sep) +3.7% y/y, as expected

scenarios.base: The dollar stays between ¥157 and ¥158 into the Fed and Bank of Japan decisions.
scenarios.bull: Firm US data and calm stocks lift the dollar above ¥158, weighing on the yen.
scenarios.bear: A stock sell-off or a hot Tokyo inflation reading sends the dollar back below ¥157.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc was steady in Asian trading, with the dollar near 0.8275 francs. There was no Swiss news, and calm stock markets gave investors little reason to seek safety in it.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Swiss National Bank holds rates at zero with inflation near zero, so the franc moves mostly on global fear; it held near a one-month high against the dollar last week. What changed: Nothing new from Switzerland. Asian stocks mostly rose and oil eased a little, so the franc held where it ended Monday. What it means: With no Swiss news, the franc follows the global mood: calm markets keep it soft against the dollar, while a flare-up in the Middle East would bring buyers back. The question to keep asking: does the calmer mood in markets last?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the UBS survey of Swiss economic expectations at 4:00 AM CT Wednesday, and the KOF economic barometer on Friday. The Swiss National Bank's next decision is December 10.

scenarios.base: The franc stays near 0.83 per dollar while markets stay calm.
scenarios.bull: Fresh Middle East attacks or a stock sell-off send investors to the franc and the dollar below 0.825 francs.
scenarios.bear: A firm Fed message and calm markets lift the dollar toward 0.83 francs.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Australian dollar edged up to near 70.3 US cents before Australia's third-quarter inflation figures at 7:30 PM CT tonight. Strong profit figures from Chinese factories, a big buyer of Australian raw materials, helped a little.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates four times this year to 4.60%, and markets see a November 3 hike as close to an even bet, which has kept the Aussie near its strongest levels of the year. What changed: Profits at Chinese factories, mines and utilities rose 14.4% from a year earlier in September, up from 4.2% in August, a plus for Australia, which sells China much of its iron ore and energy. Banks expect the trimmed-mean inflation measure to rise about 1.0% in the third quarter, above the 0.8% the Reserve Bank forecast. The Aussie rose about 0.1% to near 70.28 cents. What it means: Investors are leaning toward a hot reading. A figure at or above 1.0% would make a November hike likely and support the Aussie; a softer one would push the hike out and could undo the overnight gain. The question to keep asking: does tonight's figure make a November hike likely?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Reserve Bank of Australia officials testify to a parliamentary committee at 7:15 PM CT tonight, then the third-quarter inflation figures at 7:30 PM CT (trimmed mean about +1.0% on the quarter expected). The bank decides on November 3.
numbers: Q3 trimmed-mean forecast ~+1.0% q/q vs RBA's 0.8%

scenarios.base: The Aussie stays near 70.3 cents until the inflation figures.
scenarios.bull: A trimmed mean above 1.0% on the quarter makes a November hike likely and lifts the Aussie above 70.5 cents.
scenarios.bear: A reading of 0.8% or less pushes the hike out and pulls the Aussie below 70 cents.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie was steady near 1.401 per US dollar overnight as oil eased slightly. Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada's position in trade talks with the US has not changed, cooling hopes for a quick deal before Wednesday's Bank of Canada decision.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Canadian dollar rose for seven straight days last week, to its strongest in about a month, helped by high oil and bets that the Bank of Canada hikes on October 28 because energy is pushing inflation up. What changed: Prime Minister Mark Carney said Ottawa's position in trade talks with the US is unchanged, so hopes of a deal faded; US tariff changes on some Canadian goods take effect on October 30. Oil slipped about half a percent. The US dollar edged down to about 1.4012 Canadian. What it means: The loonie is holding up because a Bank of Canada hike is still mostly expected. Fading trade hopes and softer oil take away some support, so a hold on Wednesday would hit it harder than a hike would help. The question to keep asking: does governor Tiff Macklem hike and signal more?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Bank of Canada decision and Monetary Policy Report at 8:45 AM CT Wednesday, with governor Tiff Macklem's press conference after; Canada's August GDP comes Friday at 7:30 AM CT.

scenarios.base: The loonie stays near 1.40 per US dollar into Wednesday's decision.
scenarios.bull: A Bank of Canada hike with a signal of more, or an oil rebound, pulls the US dollar below 1.395 Canadian.
scenarios.bear: A hold, or more trade friction, lifts the US dollar above 1.41 Canadian.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi edged up to near 56.9 US cents before the Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision at 8:00 PM CT tonight, where a rate hike is widely expected.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: New Zealand's central bank is expected to raise its rate to 3.00% from 2.75% on October 28, because inflation, at 3.7%, is still above its target, and that expectation has supported the kiwi. What changed: The kiwi won back part of Monday's drop, rising to about 56.9 cents from 56.8. A majority of the NZIER Shadow Board, a panel of independent economists, backed a quarter-point hike. What it means: A hike is mostly priced, so what the bank says about further hikes matters more than the move itself. The question to keep asking: does the bank signal more hikes beyond this one?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision at 8:00 PM CT tonight, then the ANZ business confidence survey at 7:00 PM CT Wednesday.

scenarios.base: A hike to 3.00% with no strong hint keeps the kiwi near 57 cents.
scenarios.bull: A hike with a clear signal of more lifts the kiwi above 57.2 cents.
scenarios.bear: A hike framed as the last, or a surprise hold, sends the kiwi below 56.5 cents.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Brent crude eased about 0.6% to near $115 a barrel in Asian trading as regional talks with Iran continued. Fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz kept prices high.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Oil has stayed high since the US–Iran war began in February, and Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites drove Brent to a six-month high last week. What changed: Hopes for diplomacy, after envoys from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey met Iran's leaders in Tehran on Monday, pulled prices down a little further. Yemen's Houthi rebels and Saudi Arabia kept exchanging fire, and Reuters reported a record month of attacks on ships near Hormuz, which kept supply worries alive. Brent was near $115.15 and US crude near $100.80. What it means: The war premium is still mostly in the price; talk alone takes off only small amounts. High oil keeps inflation up, which supports central banks that are raising rates and hurts energy importers like Japan and the euro area. The question to keep asking: do the talks produce anything concrete?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: any result from the regional talks with Iran, the American Petroleum Institute's weekly oil stocks at 3:30 PM CT Tuesday, and official US stocks figures at 9:30 AM CT Wednesday.

scenarios.base: With no deal and no major attack, Brent holds between $112 and $118.
scenarios.bull: A confirmed hit on Saudi output or a breakdown in talks sends Brent above $118.
scenarios.bear: A concrete step toward a deal with Iran pulls Brent toward $110.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold slipped about 0.3% to near $4,020 an ounce in Asian trading, holding just above $4,000. Investors are waiting for Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Gold fell nearly 4% last week as high oil raised fears of more inflation and more US rate hikes; gold pays no interest, so it suffers when rates rise. What changed: Gold traded mostly sideways overnight, easing from about $4,033 at Monday's close to near $4,020, as the dollar held firm. What it means: Buyers are defending the $4,000 area, but the forces that pushed gold down are still in place: oil is high and a December Fed hike is still expected. The question to keep asking: what does the Federal Reserve signal about December on Wednesday?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US durable goods orders at 7:30 AM CT and consumer confidence at 9:00 AM CT Tuesday, then the Fed decision at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday and the press conference at 1:30 PM CT.

scenarios.base: Gold holds between $4,000 and $4,050 until the Fed.
scenarios.bull: Weak US figures or a Fed that sounds unsure about December lift gold above $4,050.
scenarios.bear: A Fed that clearly signals a December hike pushes gold back below $4,000.

calls.note: Brent was never near $110 at the settlement: it ended down 0.8% at about $115.81, with no attack and no breakdown in talks; early reports of a 6% fall did not hold up.

calls.text: Dollar index near 101.7 with no major US data left today: if oil keeps falling, it slips toward 101.5 by the close; an oil rebound lifts it back toward 101.8
calls.note: Oil eased only slightly, yet the dollar index rose to about 102.0 by the close, past both levels, as investors favoured the dollar before the Fed.

calls.text: Pound near $1.337 before Wednesday's UK Budget: with no UK data, it stays between $1.333 and $1.341 by the close; a Budget leak on borrowing moves it out of that range
calls.note: With no UK data and no Budget leak, the pound ended near $1.3346, inside the range.

calls.text: Brent near $114 after Aramco cleared its Dhahran headquarters: a Houthi hit that cuts Saudi output lifts Brent past its May highs and supports the loonie; a quiet weekend lets it ease toward $110
calls.note: Both happened in turn: Houthi attacks lifted Brent to about $117 on Friday without a confirmed cut to Saudi output, then a quiet weekend and talks in Tehran took it to about $110 by Monday.

calls.text: Canada retail sales Fri 7:30 AM CT (about +1.3% expected for August): a strong rebound lifts bets on Bank of Canada hikes beyond October 28; a miss keeps it to one
calls.note: Sales rose 1.2%, a touch under the 1.3% expected, so neither a strong beat nor a miss; Bank of Canada hike pricing for October 28 stayed near 75–80%.

calls.text: Brent near $112 after the Iran strike-plan report: a confirmed hit on Gulf oil output or a US move toward strikes pushes it above the $112.68 high and lifts the yen and franc; an official denial lets it slip toward $108 by the close
calls.note: Brent did top the high, to about $113, and the yen and franc gained, but without a confirmed hit or an official US move: the report alone and Iran's tanker claims did it.

calls.text: Euro-area consumer confidence 9:00 AM CT (about −17 expected) with France's gap over Germany at its widest since 2011: a weaker reading keeps the euro under $1.12; a steady one lets it recover
calls.note: The reading was weaker (−17.9), yet the euro recovered to about $1.1218 as US yields fell, so the bond rally outweighed the survey.

calls.text: US bond rally on war fears: if the 10-year yield stays near 5.05% into the close, the yen holds its gains near ¥157; if yields rebound on the strong claims figure, the dollar climbs back toward ¥158
calls.note: Yields did not rebound; they fell further, to about 4.95%, on a tech sell-off, and the yen extended its gains to about ¥156.85.

calls.text: US 10-year yield below 5% after the tech sell-off: if Asian and European stocks keep falling overnight, the yen pushes toward ¥156 and the dollar index slips under 101.5; a rebound in stocks lifts yields and the dollar back toward ¥157.5
calls.note: Asian stocks kept falling (Nikkei −1.3%) and the dollar dipped to about ¥156.3, but steadied near ¥156.9 by 12:40 AM CT; the dollar index held at about 101.5 rather than slipping under it.

calls.text: Euro-area flash business surveys Fri 3:00 AM CT (manufacturing ~52.7, services ~52.6 expected), hours before Moody's on France: misses keep the euro near $1.12; beats firm December ECB hike bets and lift it
calls.note: The surveys missed (euro-area composite 51.9, France back in contraction at 48.4), and the euro stayed near $1.12.

calls.text: US flash PMIs Fri 8:45 AM CT (services ~58.0 expected) and Michigan inflation expectations 9:00 AM CT: firm readings lift yields back toward 5% and steady the dollar; soft ones extend the bond rally
calls.note: The surveys were firm on prices and the Michigan inflation outlook ticked up; the 10-year yield rose back to about 5.00% and the dollar index firmed to about 101.8 on Friday.

calls.text: SNB policy summary 2:30 AM CT: worry about a strong franc keeps December cut bets alive and caps the franc; a calmer tone lets it firm
calls.note: Calmer tone: the bank dropped its stronger readiness to intervene and gave no December cut signal. The franc firmed slightly, with the dollar near 0.823, and hit a three-month high against the euro.

calls.text: Saudi departure order: widening across the Gulf or a hit on Saudi output puts Brent well above $110 and lifts the dollar and loonie; staying contained lets oil drift
calls.note: Brent did climb well above $110 (about $113 by the close), but on reports of US–Israeli strike plans and Iranian tanker claims, not a wider departure order. The loonie edged up; the dollar slipped.

calls.text: UK retail sales Fri 1:00 AM CT (−0.2% expected): a strong print lifts December hike bets and the pound; a weak one trims both
calls.note: Sales fell 0.4%, worse than expected, yet the pound reached its strongest against the euro since May 2025 on Friday as a November Bank of England hike stayed near certain.

calls.text: US jobless claims Thu 7:30 AM CT (about 200,000 expected): staying low keeps the Fed's December hike near 90%; a jump trims it and weighs on the dollar
calls.note: Claims stayed low at 194,000 (200,000 expected), near their lowest in decades. December hike bets held near 90% (CME FedWatch, Oct 21); a sharp bond rally later still pulled the dollar lower.

calls.text: Moody's review of France Fri: a downgrade widens France's gap over German yields and weighs on the euro; holding the rating eases the pressure
calls.note: Moody's held France at Aa3; French yields eased on Monday and the euro led the majors in the European morning.

calls.text: Bailey 8:00 AM CT after the 3.5% UK inflation print: backing November without promising more keeps the pound near $1.34; any opening to a December follow-up lifts it; calling energy temporary trims it
calls.note: Neither branch: Bailey gave no new signal on rates. The pound still held near $1.34 (about 1.3395 at the New York close), with December's second hike about a coin toss.

calls.text: US crude oil stocks 9:30 AM CT (industry survey: about −4.9M barrels): a big official draw keeps Brent above $110; a build lets the rebound fade
calls.note: The draw came (−3.1M barrels, far more than forecast) and Brent briefly topped $110.8, but it still faded to $108.82 at the settle after the US Treasury's tanker licence and emergency fuel loans.

calls.text: Pakistan's mediation after Iran's uranium refusal: any confirmed opening drains oil's premium and lifts the euro and yen; more warships and no talks keep Brent near $110 into the close
calls.note: No opening: Rubio called a deal extremely difficult and more US warships headed in. Brent settled at $108.82, near $110 but off its high on Washington's supply moves rather than diplomacy.

calls.text: Japan national CPI Thu 6:30 PM CT (2.1% expected): a hot print keeps the BoJ's December hike near three in four; a soft one fades it and weighs on the yen
calls.note: Neither branch: 2.1% exactly as expected (1.7% prior), though the measure that also leaves out energy jumped to 2.4%. December hike pricing held near 80%.

calls.text: US–Iran framework: confirmation by either government drains oil's risk premium and pulls US long yields lower; another denial puts Brent back toward $110
calls.note: No confirmation from either government, and no fresh denial either. Brent still climbed back toward $110 overnight, on tanker attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman rather than on the talks.

calls.text: RBA's Hauser 5:30 PM CT: leaning on sticky inflation keeps a November hike near 1 in 3; leaning on the softer job market trims it
calls.note: Hauser leaned on sticky inflation: the outlook is 'materially worse'. Odds of a November hike rose to about 40% from about 30%, and the Aussie hit a three-week high near 0.702.

calls.note: Beat: 4.5% vs 4.4% fc (q/q 1.2%); retail +1.1% the standout. AUD/USD +0.3-0.5% to ~0.697, the night's best G10 performer; USD/CNH 6.6811, strongest since June 2022. Two-speed beat (factories lead, property -20.6% YTD).

Correction (Oct 20): by Monday's close swaps had jumped to ~87% for an October hike on Macklem's Saturday forecast warning; the 1-in-4 figure was stale.

calls.text: UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%): 3.5%+ starts pricing a December follow-up; soft reopens Bailey's 2027 read
calls.note: Hot branch: 3.5% vs 3.4% expected (3.1% in August), the highest in 11 months. November's hike is near certain; how much December moved was not yet verified at write.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y): hot settles the RBNZ's two-way bet toward the hike side
calls.note: Not hot: inflation came in at 3.7%, a touch soft. The hike side still settled anyway, with October 28 now about 98% priced.

calls.text: Japan CPI Fri + BoJ Oct 29-30: Ueda's 'quite close' language tested — October hike stays ~25%
calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
